A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ctrl-Z Sampling work. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v2 reports original text-to-image experiments on Pick-a-Pic, DrawBench and T2I-CompBench, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and generated examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds DPM/AYS and CFG++ combination experiments, exploration-frequency measurements and intermediate sampling case studies.

M1.justification: The core adaptive reward-guided search remains. Algorithm 1 caps rollback at T-t, changes the exploration-window boundary from >= to >, and tests best_score rather than the last candidate when stopping search. Appendix C.5 also introduces solver integrations and full versus partial CFG++ variants that change which forward updates use CFG++.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three text-to-image benchmarks and compositional requirements. The additional checkpoint, solver combinations and trajectory examples do not establish new datasets, domains or task coverage.

E2.justification: The original DDIM, Resampling, Z-Sampling and SOP comparisons remain. New Tables 7–10 evaluate DPM, AYS and CFG++ against their Ctrl-Z combinations, substantially extending the evaluated comparison methods beyond approaches merely cited in v2.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings remain, but Appendix C.5 adds substantially different protocols: Stable Diffusion 1.5 with a 10-step second-order DPM/AYS schedule and exploration at every step, plus CFG++ comparisons using guidance weight 0.6. Section C.6 adds a 500-prompt diagnostic with exploration window 50, four candidates and maximum depth three.

E4.justification: Existing depth, width, threshold and initiation ablations are retained. New analyses test compatibility with alternative solvers and guidance, compare full versus partial CFG++ integration, measure exploration initiation and termination depths, and inspect intermediate trajectories and redundant late searches in Appendix F.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new exploration histograms describe search behavior rather than uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: All matched pre-existing table values remain unchanged, including the relocated Hunyuan-DiT results. New Tables 7–10 add substantial results: for example, the new SD1.5/10-step experiment reports Pick-a-Pic ImageReward of -0.145 for AYS and 0.433 for Ctrl-Z + AYS. Figures 5 and 7–11 add exploration distributions and intermediate image/reward outcomes.

T1.justification: The existing DDIM, inversion and reward-criterion mathematics are retained with notation and indexing corrections. Appendix C.5.2 presents standard CFG/CFG++ update formulas to explain the integrations; it adds no substantive theoretical derivation, proof or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive escape from local optima, generation quality, efficiency and compatibility. Changing the abstract from a 6.72-fold increase to 7.72 times the original NFEs clarifies the cost already reported in Table 1 rather than changing the underlying claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for architecture-dependent aesthetic tradeoffs and variable computation, diminished benefits under coarse solver schedules, and differences between full and partial CFG++ integration. It also discusses redundant exploration after reward saturation and explicitly leaves pixel-space applicability unvalidated. The earlier scheduling and scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies that NFEs are averaged per denoising step and documents implementation choices for the new integrations, including schedule-matched inversion and where CFG++ replaces CFG. Existing default hyperparameters, hardware and software versions were already disclosed in v2 and remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially broadens related work to distillation, parallel and speculative diffusion sampling, LLM inference scaling and verifier-guided search. Section 2 also adds pruning research. This expands the distinction between Ctrl-Z's quality-oriented inference search and approaches primarily targeting sampling speed.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted prose revisions, numbers sections and appendices, reorganizes supplementary discussions, and adds an LLM writing-assistance disclosure. The main narrative, contribution list and conclusion remain largely intact; much of the added text documents new scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, with resized and relocated displays and colored algorithm lines. v3 merges v2 Tables 2 and 4 into one main-text table and adds four experimental tables and six figures. Existing qualitative image grids are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens previously asserted compatibility through experiments, makes practical limitations clearer through exploration diagnostics, and corrects procedural inconsistencies in Algorithm 1. These improve support and clarity while retaining the original benchmark evidence. The new combination tables omit NFEs and uncertainty estimates, limiting stronger conclusions about efficiency and reliability; the overall gain is useful but limited.
